title: Multiple Leg Sling, NSN 3940-01-541-1084
description: The Multiple Leg Sling is an adjustable cargo sling system that provides capability to lift, suspend and transport cargo primarily utilized within Navy and Joint maritime logistics environments. It is designed to secure and hoist palletized unit loads during crucial replenishment maneuvers: A Multiple Leg Sling is designed to solve critical physics problems during transporting of material that is heavy and irregular shapes with a single attachment point. To do this this sling has to have multiple legs to help steady the load.

PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. Parts replacement records. Parts inspection data before and after repair as applicable. Acceptance test data. QA personnel shall maintain a complete receipt inspection,test, repair re-test, history card for each item processed. This information shall be made available to the Government upon request. 4. description: *********************THIS IS A MARKET SURVEY ONLY************************* - This is not a Screening Information Request or Request for Proposals of any kind; - The FAA is not seeking or accepting unsolicited proposals; - The FAA will not pay for any information received or costs incurred in preparing the response to the market survey; and - Any costs associated with the market survey submittal are solely at the interested vendor�s expense. - The responses to this market survey will be used for informational purposes only. This is not a Screening Information Request or Request for Proposal of any kind. The FAA is not seeking or accepting proposals at this time. ****************************************************************************** 1. This is a market survey for a construction project titled: Thomas P. Stafford Building (TPS) Restroom Upgrades at the Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center (MMAC), Oklahoma City, OK. 2. The Magnitude of Construction is between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000. Performance and payment bonds will be required in a penal sum equal to 100% of the contract price. The Thomas P. Stafford Building (TPS) at the MMAC is a 222,130 gross square foot building originally constructed in 1991 and is comprised of a basement and two floors above grade. The Thomas P. Stafford Building (Building 27) at the Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center (MMAC) in Oklahoma City functions as a state-of-the-art training complex. It houses the FAA Academy, providing advanced classrooms and simulation laboratories for air traffic control and Technical Operations students and instructors. This project will upgrade the restrooms to meet ADA compliance and will also include upgrades to the corridor finishes. Work associated with construction of this project will be done primarily after hours (Midnight 12:00 am to 6:00 am Monday through Friday) and weekends to prevent disturbance to classes while the building is occupied. The building is fully occupied and runs two shifts of classes from 6:00am to midnight 12:00am Monday through Friday. The work required for the facility will include the following: Provide all labor, equipment, and material to renovate all restrooms on all floors and to upgrade common area finishes in the Thomas P. Stafford building. Requirements will be detailed in the construction plans and specifications provided by the FAA. The project includes: Architectural Restroom Scope: Replace finishes and fixtures in bathrooms on all floors. Replace wall tile, countertops, sinks, faucets, partitions, paint ceilings and doors, new door push plates and kick plates. Provide temporary trailer restrooms to maintain current fixture counts during renovation of restrooms. Only one Men�s and one Women�s restroom in the facility shall be under construction at a time. ADA automatic door openers are to be protected during construction and/or re-installed and operational after renovation at restrooms in which they occur. Mechanical Restroom Scope: Replace supply diffusers and exhaust grilles in restrooms. Fire Sprinkler Scope: Modify fire sprinklers as required. Electrical Restroom Scope: Provide the electrical effort required to upgrade/replace the Lighting and Lighting Controls as part of the coordinated Restroom Upgrades. LD lighting shall be used for both general lighting and egress lighting with footcandle illumination levels meeting both Life Safety required code levels and IES recommended target design levels. Architectural Finishes in Common Circulation Areas Scope: Demo and replace millwork in the Snack Bar area on the first floor. Replace the flooring in the caf�. This work will take place after caf� hours. Flooring replacement to be accomplished over a long weekend and be ready for business opening the following week or at least be in a state to allow normal and sanitary operations of the caf� to continue until work is complete. Corridor walls to full height and gypsum wall board ceilings to receive new high traffic quality paint. The new finish will be applied over the existing Zolatone wall finish and above the existing wall wainscot. Accent color wall paint will be applied to areas as designated in floor plans. Painting can only occur starting Friday at midnight 12:00am but must stop by Saturday at midnight 12:00am (24 hour timeframe) to allow paint odors to dissipate on Sunday. Contractor to provide fans for ventilation to run until Sunday night. Remove circular signage at all doors and paint doors and door frames both sides. Replace with ABA/ANSI A117.1 compliant signage next to doors. Replace walk-off grating at all entrances to the building with walk-off carpeting. VCT (Vinyl Composite Tile) at corridor alcoves to be replaced. Paint all door frames and window framing gray color in place of purple. Painting both sides will require coordination with user groups and will need to be after hours work due to class schedules. Replace stair treads at four exterior staircases, new treads to include an abrasive edge to closely match what is installed at interior atrium staircases. 3. The purpose of this market survey is to solicit statements of interest and capabilities from small businesses, to include applicable small business socio-economic status, capable of providing the required construction services as well as to determine whether adequate competition exists to set-aside the competition among small businesses, to include applicable small business socio-economic status. The NAICS code applicable to this requirement is 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The business size standard for this NAICS is $45.0 million. title: FCI Leavenworth Elevator & Chairlift Maintenance Requirement
description: ELEVATOR AND CHAIRLIFT MAINTENANCE SERVICES FCI LEAVENWORTH Category: Facilities, Subcategory: Facilities Maintenance and Repair NAICS: 561210 1. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Correctional Institution Leavenworth, requests quotations from eligible contractors for elevator and chairlift maintenance services in accordance with the attached Statement of Work. The requirement covers: - One traction elevator serving the Administrative Building. - One hydraulic elevator serving the Food Service/West Storeroom. - One Garaventa GSL Artira chairlift serving the Administrative Building entrance. Services include quarterly preventive maintenance, scheduled and unscheduled repairs, emergency callback services, service reporting, and annual inspection support as specified in the final SOW. The Government anticipates issuing one firm-fixed-price task order with a 12-month base period and four 12-month option periods. Place of Performance: FCI Leavenworth 1300 Metropolitan Avenue Leavenworth, Kansas 66048 Period of Performance - Base Period: January 1, 2027 - December 31, 2027 Option Year 1: January 1, 2028 - December 31, 2028 Option Year 2: January 1, 2029 - December 31, 2029 Option Year 3: January 1, 2030 - December 31, 2030 Option Year 4: January 1, 2031 - December 31, 2031 2. QUOTATION SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Submit quotations by the closing date and time identified in this RFQ to Contract Specialist, Kathleen Wood, kwood1@bop.gov. Quotations must include the following: A. Contractor Information Provide: - Legal business name, business address, and UEI. - Point of contact, telephone number, and email address. - Quotation validity period. - Acknowledgment of all solicitation amendments. B. Technical Service Approach Submit a technical service approach of no more than three pages addressing: 1. Equipment capability: Explain the ability to maintain and repair the traction elevator, hydraulic elevator, and Garaventa chairlift identified in the SOW. 2. Maintenance and inspection support: Describe the approach to quarterly preventive maintenance, service scheduling, reporting, and annual inspection support. 3. Staffing continuity: Describe qualified primary and backup technician coverage, availability during absences or concurrent service calls, and any subcontracting arrangements. 4. Emergency response: Explain the dispatch arrangements and available resources supporting the SOW's one-hour response requirement for trapped individuals and two-hour response requirement for other outages. 5. Parts and technical support: Explain access to necessary replacement parts, diagnostic tools, and technical support. 6. Institution coordination: Explain coordination of technician approvals, backup personnel, institution entry, escorts, tool control, and service scheduling. Provide a practical explanation of how the services will be performed. A general statement agreeing to comply with the SOW does not adequately describe the proposed approach. C. Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of similar services performed within the past five years, including ongoing work. Government, commercial, and relevant subcontract performance may be submitted. For each example, provide: - Customer and project name. - Contract or order number, if available. - Performance dates. - Equipment and services covered. - Contractor's role. - Relevant performance results, including service reliability, emergency response, and resolution of performance problems. - Customer reference name, business email, and telephone number. Limit each example to one page. Contractors without relevant past performance should state that fact. D. Pricing: Complete the pricing schedule below for the base period and all four option periods. Provide one annual firm-fixed price for each period covering all three units and all services included in the final SOW. Include all necessary labor, supervision, equipment, tools, travel, reporting, included repairs and parts, emergency callbacks, and inspection support. Identify any exceptions or proposed exclusions. Do not assume that contractor standard service-agreement exclusions apply. - Base Period: - Option Year 1: - Option Year 2: - Option Year 3: - Option Year 4: - E. Page Limits The three-page technical limit excludes contractor identification, past-performance examples, pricing, required representations, amendment acknowledgments, and exceptions. Use readable text of at least 11 points on standard letter-size pages. Technical pages exceeding the three-page limit will not be evaluated. Do not place additional technical narrative in excluded sections to circumvent the limit. 3. EVALUATION AND BASIS FOR SELECTION The Government will select the eligible Schedule contractor whose quotation meets the solicitation requirements and provides the best value considering: 1. Technical Service Approach. 2. Past Performance. 3. Price. Technical Service Approach is more important than Past Performance. Together, the nonprice factors are more important than Price. A. Technical Service Approach The Government will evaluate how well the proposed approach demonstrates the ability to maintain the identified equipment and meet the SOW. Considerations include equipment familiarity; maintenance and inspection-support planning; qualified primary and backup staffing; credible emergency dispatch and response coverage; access to parts and diagnostic support; and coordination with institution access requirements. These considerations explain the technical factor and are not separately weighted subfactors. B. Past Performance The Government will evaluate the relevance and quality of available past-performance information, including maintenance reliability, emergency response, and resolution of service problems. The Government may obtain information from submitted references, CPARS where applicable, and other available sources. A contractor without relevant past performance, or for whom sufficient information is unavailable, will not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably solely because of that absence. C. Price The Government will evaluate the sum of the base-period price and all four option-period prices. All quotations must address the same final SOW requirements. Evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise them. D. Comparative Evaluation The Government will compare quotations directly against the stated evaluation factors and one another to identify meaningful differences and determine which quotation provides the best value. Numerical scores and adjectival ratings will not be assigned. The selection will be supported by a narrative explaining the material differences and their importance to successful performance. The Government may select a higher-priced quotation when its benefits warrant the additional price. The Government may select a lower-priced quotation when additional benefits do not justify a higher price. The Government intends to make its selection based on initial quotations but may communicate with contractors or request revised quotations when appropriate. Contractors should submit their best technical and pricing terms initially. 4. SITE VISIT Date and Time: December 1, 2026 at 10:00 AM Registration Deadline: November 25, 2026 at 3:00 PM Reporting Location: FCI Leavenworth, 1300 Metropolitan Ave. Leavenworth, KS 66048 A. Purpose and Attendance The Government will conduct a site visit to allow prospective quoters to observe the covered equipment and become familiar with the service locations, equipment conditions, and institution access requirements. Attendance is encouraged but is not mandatory and will not be evaluated as a condition of award. Contractors remain responsible for submitting quotations addressing the entire solicitation and SOW. B. Registration and Access Approval Register with [contracting contact and email] by the registration deadline. Provide the company name, attendee names, and a business telephone

title: FCI Oxford - Water Softener
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) and the Federal Correctional Institution Oxford located at 350 Elk Avenue, Oxford, Wisconsin, intend to make a single award to a responsible entity that will provide all necessary equipment, labor, materials, and incidentals to remove existing water softeners and install a new centralized water softener for the entire Institution. Awarded Contractor shall provide materials, labor, and equipment to remove existing water softeners, pipe through and install a new centralized water softener and all associated components. FCI Oxford currently has several commercial-grade water softeners which are failing to efficiently reduce water hardness and protect water systems, as well as connected equipment. The new centralized system should improve water quality, minimize calcium buildup, and extend the service life of plumbing infrastructure and appliances. The contractor would place a brine tank and softener to be installed at the water tower. Water would be treated right off the water main, therefore there would be no need for bagged salt to be brought in weekly.

title: MORIAH WIND SYSTEM (MWS)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION - SOURCES SOUGHT NAVAL AIR WARFARE CENTER, AIRCRAFT DIVISION LAKEHURST, NJ MORIAH WIND SYSTEM (MWS) THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued pursuant to FAR 15.201(e). This RFI is for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or promise to issue a solicitation in the future. It is a Market Research tool being used to identify potential technologies and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWC-AD) Lakehurst is seeking to continue the production of the U.S. Fleet wind systems for program management, production, systems engineering, logistics support and acceptance for the Moriah Wind System (MWS). The MWS program produces multiple configurations and variants of the MWS and associated components. A description of the Moriah Wind System follows: MWS provides digital wind speed and direction information, including crosswind and headwind, that supports decision making for air operations, combat, navigation, tactical planning and firefighting. The MWS replaces legacy Type F Wind Measuring and Indicating and Digital Wind Systems (DWS), providing a single wind measuring system, consistent across all ship classes, Land Based Test Site, and shore stations. MWS consists of the following main parts: Ultrasonic Wind Sensor Unit (WSU) with non-moving parts Wind Processor unit (WPU) consisting of dual redundant processors capable of interfacing with legacy wind and ship systems and Shipboard Local Area Networks (LANs) High-End Display (HED) with full range of available wind information and ship speed/ course data, including the display of Aircraft Recovery Bulletins (ARBs), Launch and Recovery Envelopes (LREs) and Final Course data. The HED is hardwired to one of the WSUs in a safety critical configuration to enable the display of wind data when the WPU or another connecting network is not functioning. HED fits inside an envelope no larger than11.50� high by 18.00� wide by 9.53� deep. This does not include maintenance access, connector access or environmental excursions. HED must be NVD compatible. Low-End Display (LED) with basic wind information and ship speed/course data. LED fits inside an envelope no larger than 7.36� high by 11.10� wide by 6.06� deep. This does not include maintenance access, connector access or environmental excursions. LED must be NVD compatible. The Air Temperature and Humidity Sensor (ATHU) is an accurate self-contained instrument for measuring external air temperature and humidity. The sensor electronics are enclosed in ruggedized stainless-steel housing. The Air Pressure Unit (APU) is an accurate self-contained instrument for measuring external air pressure. The sensor element and all associated electronics to produce a unidirectional serial data interface are housed in a cast aluminum box. The WSUs, HEDs and LEDs are uniform across ship classes, land-based test sites, and shore stations, with the quantity of each item dependent upon ship class/shore location. Every MWS has one WPU with dual-redundant processors, which will differ depending upon ship class and shore station either of which can individually perform all the functions necessary to keep MWS running. The sub-processors communicate with each other directly and periodically to determine functional status and to allow changes in control when a failure is detected. MWS accesses unclassified data only. There is a degree of system-to-system information exchange in MWS. Neither MWS nor its components are connected to the Global Information Grid (GIG). MWS data is output from its WPU in several ways: 1) synchro interfaces to provide wind information to legacy systems (SLQ-32, SPN-46, Integrated Launch and Recovery Television System (ILARTS), and Arresting Gear Crosscheck System); 2) serial and network interfaces for output of wind, navigational and system information to displays; and 3) network interfaces to communicate wind information to other ship systems and MWS displays. Currently, MWS will communicate over Aviation Data Management and Control System (ADMACS) on CVNs, through Digital Multiplex System (DMS) on DDGs and on a MWS controlled network on all other ship classes. Wind data is transmitted in the standard message format and protocol (SMF&P) data format and the National Marine Electronics Association (NMEA) data format. MWS receives the ARBs it displays through ADMACS via Network File System (NFS). MWS displays LREs that are programmed into the HEDs. In order to display ship�s speed and direction, calculate true wind speed and direction, as well as pitch and roll, MWS receives a data packet from Navigation Sensor System Interface (NAVSSI), which contains a host of navigational data, including ship�s positional information. MWS does not use any of this other information, although it must read the entire NAVSSI data packet prior to extracting the data required. The information in this packet is not sensitive unless the information is transmitted off the ship. However, MWS has no mechanism for transmitting data off the ship, nor any requirement to do so. MWS uses strictly defined data types for transmission into and out of the system. This information is limited to either NMEA ASCII strings using checksums to determine data integrity, structured binary data format using checksums to determine data integrity, proprietary DMS Light Internet Protocol (DLIP), and analog synchro resolver output to other ship systems. The data items themselves are confined to information from known systems (as defined in the relevant Interface Requirements Specifications) or is confined to IP addresses and ports specified in the Interface Design Documents (IDD) and the network architecture (ADMACS, DMS or other ship network). The components contain no TELNET or File Transfer Protocol (FTP) capability. Configuration is done via a manual procedure where a MWS cyber accredited laptop is attached to the system components using a serial cable (RS-422) and programming is done via contractor supplied software applications. The processor software was written to run under a tailored Linux Operating System with minimal functionality on an Intel/ARM platform. This operating system consists of a Linux kernel that has been built specifically for use in this environment that will aid security. It contains only those device drivers and services that are relevant to this embedded environment. Software design protects system integrity by the fact that unauthorized personnel do not have the ability to modify the software configuration, data or application. MWS is not designed for use or visibility on the internet and there is no access to the internet. MWS uses UDP/IP & TCP/IP for unicast and multicast communication protocols. NAWC-AD Lakehurst is requesting information from industry for the purpose of identifying qualified contractors interested in producing MWS. The objective of this is to continue production of the following MWS parts, which establish the current MWS configuration baseline: P/N Nomenclature P/N 81164/0200.00 Wind Sensor Unit (WSU) P/N 82374-0200-00 Wind Sensor Unit (WSU) P/N 81161/0200.00/E High End Display (HED) P/N 82371-0200-00-E High End Display (HED) P/N 81162/0200.00/E Low End Display (LED) P/N 82372-0200-00-E Low End Display (LED) P/N 81161/0102.00 HED LED GUI KIT P/N 82371-0102-00 HED LED GUI KIT P/N 81163/0102.00 WPU GUI KIT P/N 81163/0200.00W01 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V1 P/N 82373-0200-00W01 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V1 P/N 81163/0200.00W04 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V3 P/N 82373-0200-00W04 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V3 P/N 81163/0200.00W05 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V5 P/N 81163/0200.00W06 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V6 P/N 82373-0200-00W07 Wind Processor Unit (WPU) V7 P/N PS753 28 VDC Power Supply P/N 81163/0300.00W04 WPU Sub-Processor Unit (SPU) Fiber-optic P/N 82

title: FCI Oxford - Water Softener
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) and the Federal Correctional Institution Oxford located at 350 Elk Avenue, Oxford, Wisconsin, intend to make a single award to a responsible entity that will provide all necessary equipment, labor, materials, and incidentals to remove existing water softeners and install a new centralized water softener for the entire Institution. Awarded Contractor shall provide materials, labor, and equipment to remove existing water softeners, pipe through and install a new centralized water softener and all associated components. FCI Oxford currently has several commercial-grade water softeners which are failing to efficiently reduce water hardness and protect water systems, as well as connected equipment. The new centralized system should improve water quality, minimize calcium buildup, and extend the service life of plumbing infrastructure and appliances. The contractor would place a brine tank and softener to be installed at the water tower. Water would be treated right off the water main, therefore there would be no need for bagged salt to be brought in weekly.

title: FCI Oxford - Water Softener
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) and the Federal Correctional Institution Oxford located at 350 Elk Avenue, Oxford, Wisconsin, intend to make a single award to a responsible entity that will provide all necessary equipment, labor, materials, and incidentals to remove existing water softeners and install a new centralized water softener for the entire Institution. Awarded Contractor shall provide materials, labor, and equipment to remove existing water softeners, pipe through and install a new centralized water softener and all associated components. FCI Oxford currently has several commercial-grade water softeners which are failing to efficiently reduce water hardness and protect water systems, as well as connected equipment. The new centralized system should improve water quality, minimize calcium buildup, and extend the service life of plumbing infrastructure and appliances. The contractor would place a brine tank and softener to be installed at the water tower. Water would be treated right off the water main, therefore there would be no need for bagged salt to be brought in weekly.

description: The Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs (CDMRP) seeks feedback to inform the fiscal year 2027 (FY27) Alzheimer�s Research Program (AZRP) research focus areas and associated research funding opportunities. Although FY27 federal funds have not yet been appropriated, the AZRP is collecting this information solely to support strategic program planning. This inquiry does not commit the program to incorporating this feedback into FY27 or any future AZRP funding opportunities. This RFI should not be construed as a solicitation or an obligation on the part of the AZRP or the Department of War (DoW). The CDMRP AZRP�s vision is to mitigate the impact of Alzheimer's and related dementias associated with TBI, military, and diverse risks. The AZRP�s mission is to fund impactful, solution-oriented research to address critical needs and improve quality of life for Service Members, Veterans, their Families, and the public who are living with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. Appropriations for the AZRP from FY11-26 totaled $228 million. As of October 2026, FY27 funds for the AZRP have not been appropriated. title: Q301 - Notice of Intent to Sole-Source Veracyte Decipher Testing Services - Cleveland OH VAMC
description: Notice of Intent to Sole-Source Requirement The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 10, intends to negotiate a sole source contract under Simplified Acquisition Procedures and the authority of FAR 6.302-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The associated NAICS code for this is 621511, Size Standard is $41.5M annaul receipts. Product Service Code (PSC) is Q301. The sole-source contract will be awarded to: VERACYTE, INC UEI: JS7GBP6LCMN6 Description of equipment requirements: The VA Northeast Ohio Healthcare System (VANEOHS) requires continued access to specialized genomic classifier testing used to assess risk of metastasis or metastatic progression in patients with localized or advanced prostate cancer. Decipher prostate testing is a powerful diagnostic and prognostic tool that assesses risk of prostate cancer progression within the next five years post detection, biopsy or surgical removal. The test utilizes a genome-wide transcriptome assay to analyze the expression of 22 genes to generate the Decipher score. Performed on existing tissue samples obtained during biopsy or surgical removal of the prostate, prior to any radiation or hormone therapy. Indicated in localized, N1, or metastatic disease. Provides the Decipher score based on genomic characteristics of the tumor, independent of clinical and pathological factors. The score, ranging between 0 and 1, reflects tumor aggressiveness. It is the Government's belief that only the proposed candidate possesses the required capabilities to successfully meet this requirement. It is the Government's intention to solicit and negotiate with only this source. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. IAW FAR 5.207 all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. This is not a solicitation or request for offers. No solicitation package is available. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that demonstrates the ability to comply with the requirement and that competition would be advantageous to the Government. The Government will not pay for information submitted. A determination not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responses to this intent to sole source must be emailed to Thomas Bellamy: thomas.bellamy@va.gov & Samantha Jarrett: samantha.jarrett@va.gov by 4:00 p.m. EST November 12th, 2026.

title: KFO VAULT TOILET PUMPING
description: Vault pumping services at designated recreation sites within the Kemmerer Field Office. The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, equipment, materials, water, transportation, and disposal services necessary to pump, clean, disinfect, and properly dispose of liquid and solid waste from vault toilets and associated facilities. Services will be performed at remote locations and require specialized equipment, including a minimum 1,000-gallon septic tank truck or equivalent, vacuum pump, and appropriate hoses and cleaning equipment. title: Lithuania – Travel agency, tour operator and tourist assistance services – Lietuvos Respublikos aplinkos ministerijos darbuotojų tarnybinių kelionių į užsienį organizavimo paslaugos
description: Perkamos šios Lietuvos Respublikos aplinkos ministerijos darbuotojų (ir esant poreikiui – ministerijai pavaldžių įstaigų darbuotojų ruošiantis Lietuvos pirmininkavimui Europos Sąjungos Tarybai ir Lietuvos pirmininkavimo Europos Sąjungos Tarybai laikotarpiu iki 2027-07-01) tarnybinių kelionių į užsienį organizavimo paslaugos (atskirai arba kartu) (toliau – paslaugos): 1.1. kelionės oro transportu organizavimo paslaugos; 1.2. kelionės sausumos ir vandens transportu (autobusų, traukinių ir vandens transporto bilietų rezervavimo ir pardavimo paslaugos, transporto nuomos ir transporto organizavimo nuo oro uosto iki viešbučio paslaugos ir kitos panašios paslaugos) organizavimo paslaugos; 1.3. viešbučio rezervavimo ir apgyvendinimo jame organizavimo paslaugos; 1.4. kelionės draudimo pardavimo paslaugos; 1.5. vizų ir kitų kelionei būtinų dokumentų įforminimo bei išdavimo organizavimo paslaugos. Paslaugas planuoja pirkti pagal poreikį. Numatomų paslaugų orientacinė apimtis ~ 1500 kelionių per 36 mėnesius nuo sutarties įsigaliojimo dienos. Preliminariai numatoma 1500 tarnybinių kelionių užsienyje oro transportu, 1500 apgyvendinimo paslaugų užsienyje, 1500 kelionės draudimo paslaugų, 85 vizų įforminimo paslaugos ir kt. paslaugų per 36 mėnesius. Galimi apimčių nuokrypiai didėjimo ar mažėjimo linkme. Iš viso paslaugų bus perkama už ne daugiau kaip 2 500 000,00 Eur su PVM (maksimali bendra pirkimo sutarties vertė) per 36 mėnesius nuo sutarties įsigaliojimo dienos. Perkančioji organizacija neįsipareigoja įsigyti paslaugų už maksimalią bendrą pirkimo sutarties vertę.

For the purposes of this notice HRSA is seeking industry and small business feedback to: Understand the types of businesses including small businesses who are capable of fulfilling the requirement. For small businesses, this notice seeks to specifically identify capable 8a, HUBZone, SDVOSBs, WOSB and other small businesses. Assess the feasibility of transitioning some or all of these services to a performance-based Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) structure , consistent with Executive Order 14402, Promoting Efficiency, Accountability, and Performance in Federal Contracting, dated April 30, 2026, which establishes fixed-price contracts with performance-based considerations as the default and preferred method of Federal procurement, to the maximum extent consistent with law. This Notice seeks industry feedback regarding whether the requirement, in whole or in part, is sufficiently defined to permit realistic FFP pricing and reasonable allocation of performance and cost risk. HRSA also seeks feedback regarding alternative or hybrid contract structures where FFP may not be appropriate for portions of the requirement, as well as performance measures, pricing methodology, workload assumptions, transition requirements, and small business capability. Obtain general feedback on the CICP requirement. The Government may use the information received to refine the acquisition strategy, Performance Work Statement (PWS), Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE), Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP), and any future solicitation. The Government is seeking sufficient information to support these acquisition-planning decisions and is not requesting proposals at this time.

title: Taxiway Centerline Lights
description: Notice of intent to use a brand name product. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Pacific (NAVFAC Pacific) is conducting market research in accordance with FAR Part 10 to identify potential manufacturers capable of producing taxiway centerline lights that has equal performance and listing/approval requirements as the ADB Safegate Reliance 2 (Part Number Bi Straight GG, Bi Curve GG, Uni Straight G, and Omni G) that is manufactured by ADB Safegate. Responses from third-party distributors pass through resellers, or supply brokers who do not directly own the production line or manufacturing rights to a qualified equivalent product will not be considered responsive to this market survey. FY26 Project WWXT240800 Multi-Purpose Apron and Taxiway, located on Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) Base Tindal (TDL), Australia requires taxiway centerline lighting that demonstrates the following salient characteristics: Taxiway centerline light types must have photometric performance characteristics in accordance with the requirements of Part 139 MOS, ICAO Annex 14 and DASDRM Section 6 and must exactly match the photometric performance of other LED taxiway centreline lights installed on the Aerodrome, namely lights installed on parallel Taxiway Alpha. Taxiway centerline lights must have compatibility of components with other LED taxiway centerline lights installed on the Aerodrome to facilitate interchangeability and maintenance per the requirements of the Department of Defence policy Handbook of Infrastructure Engineering � Aerodromes (HIE-A) Taxiway centerline lights must be compatible with the existing light base types ADBSG Reliance 8 inch (Part Number RSAM301P3NYNM101) to ensure interchangeability and that the mechanical performance off the fittings are compliant with the requirements of FAA Advisory Circular No. 150/5345-46 This is not a request for proposals, quotes, or an invitation for bid. The intent of this notice is to identify potential alternative taxiway centerline lights that will satisfy agency requirements. To be considered, please submit detailed technical data in order for the Government to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of your product to ensure compatibility with the existing system. In accordance with FAR 15.101(c)(2), a response to this notice is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The responder is solely responsible for the information it submits and any associated costs. The Government reserves the right to disregard any submittal that is incomplete or vague. Please do not submit company brochures. Please submit complete information via email to Ms. Josie Damo-Agcaoili via electronic mail at josie.g.damo-agcaoili.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 04 December 2026 at 12:00 p.m. H.S.T. All proprietary or classified information will be treated appropriately.

title: Bravo Dive Boat 65DS1101
description: AMENDMENT 0003 POSTED 11/26. AMENDMENT 0002 POSTED 11/21. AMENDMENT 0001 POSTED 11/19. The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish the maintenance, repair, and preservation in support of one (1) 65 FT BRAVO DIVE BOAT 65DS1101. Work will be accomplished at the Contractor's facility. Geographical Area of consideration: To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. 65DS1101 Length: 69 FT 10 IN Width: 22 FT 0 IN Draft: 3 FT 6 IN Full Displacement: 55 L TONS Age: 13 YEARS Light Load: 8,000 lbs Hull Type: Aluminum Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR) to deliver the vessel to the Contractor�s facility from Puget Sound Naval Shipyard (PSNS) Bremerton, WA. Remove all fendering and sweep blast clean. Accomplish survey of hull to identify and repair corrosion, preserve the exterior above and below the waterline, including the crane. Apply nonskid to horizontal surfaces on the exterior and interior of the boat. Replace motor mounts. Remove, inspect and install shafting, rudders and propellers. HVAC repair. Maintain and repair watertight hatches and doors. Repair, modify and preserve push knee. Replace and modify corroded deck and bulkhead structure in the main cabin. Install remote fuel shut offs. Identify and repair corrosion beneath the transformers in the aft lazzarette, install a weather shield above the starboard transformer in the aft lazzarette. Replace hydraulic, and fuel hoses. Identify and repair corroded structure beneath the shower room drain. Remove windows, repair window heaters, and reinstall windows. Replace fire suppression system piping and recertify system. Repair damage to the port bow. Accomplish modification and repair of swim platform stairs. Restore preservation system on the console in the pilot house. Replace existing generators with supplied Kohler generators, Modify, repair and install fendering system. Modify and repair the monkey heater system. Remove, inspect, preserve and install rudders. Replace thru hull valves and flexible hoses. Replace false bulkheads in the shower room and head. Open, clean and inspect all tanks. Perform sea trials after completion of repairs and full cure time of preservation. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the COR. The Period of Performance is expected to be 25 March 2026 to 29 May 2026. title: Bravo Dive Boat 65DS1101
description: AMENDMENT 0002 POSTED 11/21. AMENDMENT 0001 POSTED 11/19. The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish the maintenance, repair, and preservation in support of one (1) 65 FT BRAVO DIVE BOAT 65DS1101. Work will be accomplished at the Contractor's facility. Geographical Area of consideration: To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. 65DS1101 Length: 69 FT 10 IN Width: 22 FT 0 IN Draft: 3 FT 6 IN Full Displacement: 55 L TONS Age: 13 YEARS Light Load: 8,000 lbs Hull Type: Aluminum Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR) to deliver the vessel to the Contractor�s facility from Puget Sound Naval Shipyard (PSNS) Bremerton, WA. Remove all fendering and sweep blast clean. Accomplish survey of hull to identify and repair corrosion, preserve the exterior above and below the waterline, including the crane. Apply nonskid to horizontal surfaces on the exterior and interior of the boat. Replace motor mounts. Remove, inspect and install shafting, rudders and propellers. HVAC repair. Maintain and repair watertight hatches and doors. Repair, modify and preserve push knee. Replace and modify corroded deck and bulkhead structure in the main cabin. Install remote fuel shut offs. Identify and repair corrosion beneath the transformers in the aft lazzarette, install a weather shield above the starboard transformer in the aft lazzarette. Replace hydraulic, and fuel hoses. Identify and repair corroded structure beneath the shower room drain. Remove windows, repair window heaters, and reinstall windows. Replace fire suppression system piping and recertify system. Repair damage to the port bow. Accomplish modification and repair of swim platform stairs. Restore preservation system on the console in the pilot house. Replace existing generators with supplied Kohler generators, Modify, repair and install fendering system. Modify and repair the monkey heater system. Remove, inspect, preserve and install rudders. Replace thru hull valves and flexible hoses. Replace false bulkheads in the shower room and head. Open, clean and inspect all tanks. Perform sea trials after completion of repairs and full cure time of preservation. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the COR. The Period of Performance is expected to be 25 March 2026 to 29 May 2026. This is a 100% Small Business set-aside under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 336611, size standard 1,300 employees. All offerors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) to receive award of Government contracts. Offerors are advised also that SAM representations and certifications can be completed electronically via the System for Award Management website at https://www.sam.gov. NOTE 1: Please pay particular attention to the inclusion of DFARS 252.232-7998 Obligations in Advance of Fiscal Year 2026 Funding (DEVIATION 2026-O0001). NOTE 2: Please review Request for Quote instructions regarding contract financing.

title: C--Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) 3DNTM
description: This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) is issued to provide an opportunity to partner with the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) and other Federal agencies to acquire high-resolution 3D elevation and hydrography mapping data through the 3DNTM Data Collaboration Announcement (DCA). The 3DNTM DCA partnerships efficiently and effectively leverage funding to respond to the documented and growing need for high-quality elevation and hydrography data, which significantly benefit Americans across an array of applications like infrastructure planning, discovery of critical minerals, energy development, and disaster preparation and response for severe weather events, earthquakes, landslides, and other emergencies. Project submissions are invited from applicants who wish to partner through the 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) opportunity or the 3D Hydrography Program (3DHP) opportunity to fund lidar or hydrography data acquisition through the USGS Geospatial Products and Services Contract (GPSC). Federal agencies, state and local governments, tribes, academic institutions, and the private sector are eligible to submit projects. The Government will review applications based on the evaluation criteria identified in section VII of this opportunity. A synopsis of previous 3DNTM DCA Awards is available on https://usgs.gov/3DNTM/DCA. 3DEP and 3DHP products and services, including data resulting from this opportunity can be accessed via The National Map Data Download and Visualization Services: https://apps.nationalmap.gov.

title: Port of Aalborg Logistics A/S - Udbud af hydraulisk kran 2026 - Offentligt udbud
description: Ovennævnte udbud af én (1) hydraulisk kran gennemføres af Servicemægleren A/S på vegne af Port of Aalborg Logistics A/S som et offentligt udbud med henblik på indgåelse af én kontrakt.Kranen skal leveres, installeres og idriftsættes på Kaj 8005 – Aalborg Havn – Landdybet, 9220 Aalborg Øst.Udbuddet omfatter indkøb af én (1) diesel/HVO-drevet hydraulisk kran på gummihjulsmonteret undervogn. Den skal fortrinsvis anvendes til losning og lastning af skibe og til håndtering af bulkvarer, stykgods, biomasse og skrot på Ordregivers havneområde. Formålet er hurtig og præcis håndtering, så havnens gennemløbshastighed er høj, og skibenes liggetid er kort. title: Germany – Switching station installation work – Gebäudeautomation (KG 480)
description: Das Museum für Hamburgische Geschichte am Holstenwall 24 in Hamburg wurde zwischen 1914 und 1922 errichtet und steht unter Denkmalschutz. Im Rahmen der aktuellen Baumaßnahme erfolgt eine grundlegende Sanierung und Neustrukturierung der Ausstellungsbereiche sowie eine Erneuerung der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung. Das Gebäude umfasst folgende Hauptnutzungen: Tiefparterre: Funktions- und Lagerflächen, Werkstätten, Restaurierungsräume, Büroflächen, Depots, Küchen- und Technikflächen (Heizung/Kälte, Raumlufttechnik, Sanitär, Elektro). // Erdgeschoss: Flächen für Sonder- und Wechselausstellungen, Gastronomie mit Küche, Foyer, Shop und Veranstaltungsbereich.//1. und 2. Obergeschoss: Bereiche für Ausstellungen sowie Verwaltungsräume. Dachgeschoss: Weitere Ausstellungsflächen, Verwaltungsbereiche, Lager- und Werkstatträume. Der Bau erfolgt über zwei Bauabschnitte die wie folgt aufgeteilt sind: Ausstellung - Hier gehören die Tiefparterre, Ausstellungsräume und das Dachgeschoss. // Verwaltung - sind es die Büros und das Foyer, diese sind unterteilt in der linken und rechten von der Gebäudestruktur. Das Museum für Hamburgische Geschichte erhält eine Neugestaltung der Ausstellungsräume. In diesem Zuge wird die technische Gebäudeausrüstung inklusive der Gebäudeautomation komplett erneuert. Im Rahmen der Baumaßnahme soll eine neue Gebäudeautomation zur Regelung und Überwachung der Gewerke: Sanitär, Heizung, Kühlung, Lüftung und Elektro aufgebaut werden. Als Kommunikationsstandard ist BACnet IP zu verwenden. Die Gebäudeautomation für das MHG soll über einen Bedienrechner überwacht werden können, dieser befindet sich im Gebäude und soll über verschiedene Zugriffsebnen verfügen. Je nach Kenntnis- und Wissensstand des Nutzers können Anlagen nur angeschaut, Sollwerte und Zeitschaltprogramme angepasst/verändert oder eigene Anpassungen an der Programmierung vorgenommen werden. Die Maßnahme Gebäudeautomation umfasst den Aufbau eines eigenen GA-Netzwerkes zum Austausch der Informationen, die Bereitstellung und Montage der Feldgeräte (ausgenommen wasserseitige Montage, z. B. am Heizungsverteiler), die GA-Leitungsverlegung, die Montage und Aufstellung von den GA-Schaltschränken und den Etagenverteilern, die Programmierung, die Erstellung der Anlagenbilder, das Einrichten des Bedienrechners, die Weiterleitung der Alarmmeldungen, sowie die Inbetriebnahme, die Einweisung des Nutzers und die Dokumentation. Die Ausführung erfolgt unter enger Abstimmung mit den beteiligten TGA-Gewerken und dem Hochbau. Koordinationsleistungen sind Bestandteil der ausgeschriebenen Leistungen. Für das MHG sind drei GA-Schaltschränke (Automationsschwerpunkte, ASPs) im Untergeschoss geplant für die Überwachung und Regelung der Trinkwasserversorgung, der Heizungsanlage, der Kälteanlagen, der Lüftungsanlagen (diese verfügen über eine eigene Reglung, welche auf die GA aufgeschaltet wird) und der Elektro-Anlagen, z. B.: Casambi-Beleuchtung, Sicherheitsbeleuchtung und Brandmeldeanlage. Vom Erdgeschoss bis in das Dachgeschoss sind insgesamt 14 Etagenverteiler geplant, diese nehmen die Meldungen in den jeweiligen Etagen auf und leiten diese über das eigene GA-Netzwerk an die GA-Schalschränke weiter. Die Etagenverteiler verarbeiten Meldungen von zum Beispiel: Brandschutzklappen, Referenzfühlern und Ventilen der Wandtemperierung, Beleuchtungen der Casambi-Module oder Zählerstände von M-Bus Zählern. Besondere Rahmenbedingungen - Arbeiten innerhalb des Bestandsgebäudes - Ausführung in offener und geschlossener Bauweise - Abstimmung mit parallel tätigen Ausbau-, Hochbau- und TGA-Gewerken - Nachweis der Funktion durch Prüfprotokolle, Probebetrieb und Tests mit dem späteren Nutzer Wesentliche Arbeiten - Aufbau eines GA-Netzwerks - Lieferung und teilweise Montage der Feldgeräte - GA-Leitungsverlegung, gemeinsame Nutzung der Haupttrassen mit Elektro - Montage und Lieferung der drei GA-Schaltschränken und 14 Etagenverteiler - Programmierung und Inbetriebnahme

title: Germany – Supervision of building work – Schönfließer Brücke - Bauoberleitung und Bauüberwachung sowie Besondere Leistungen
description: Das Vorhaben besteht darin, die vorhandene Schönfließer Behelfsbrücke, die derzeit ausschließlich dem Fußverkehr dient, durch eine breitere Fuß- und Radwegbrücke am Standort der ursprünglichen Straßenbrücke zwischen Sonnenburger Straße und Schönfließer Straße zu ersetzen. Die Behelfsbrücke hat gemäß der letzten Hauptprüfung (Prüfbericht2025E/Zustandsbericht von 2026) eine Zustandsnote von 3,2. Die Erneuerung erfolgt nicht hauptsächlich aufgrund des schlechten Bauwerkszustands, sondern aufgrund der ungenügenden verkehrlichen Situation. Aufgrund der hohen täglichen Nutzung sind die Verkehrsflächen neu geordnet und eine klare Trennung von Geh- und Radverkehr auf dem neuen Bauwerk geschaffen. Zudem wird die neue Brücke für Rettungsfahrzeuge freigegeben werden. Der Neubau wird daher in der Flucht der ehemaligen Straßenbrücke errichtet, um eine direkte und befahrbare Anbindung sicherzustellen. Auf der parallel verlaufenden Kabel- und Leitungsbrücke kam es im Jahr 2021 zu einem Brand, der das Tragwerk beschädigte. Das Bauwerk muss daher bis spätestens 2028 außer Betrieb genommen werden. Der Senat verfolgt das Ziel, beide bisherigen Bauwerke zu einem einzigen, leistungsfähigen Neubau zusammenzuführen und sämtliche Kabel- und Leitungen in die neue Brücke zu integrieren. Die bestehende Behelfsbrücke wird anschließend zurückgebaut.

description: Die Auftraggeber, der Landesbetrieb SBH I Schulbau Hamburg (SBH) sowie GMH I Gebäudemanagement Hamburg GmbH (GMH) – ein öffentliches Unternehmen der FHH - sind zuständig für den Bildungsbau und betreuen etwa die Hälfte der öffentlichen Gebäude der Freien und Hansestadt Hamburg. SBH I Schulbau Hamburg und die GMH Gebäudemanagement Hamburg GmbH haben sich unter dem Dach von Bildungsbau Hamburg zu den Spezialisten für den Schulbau und das Management kommunaler Immobilien, Sportimmobilien und Hochschulen in Hamburg entwickelt. SBH hat die Aufgabe, die Schulen und schulnahe Immobilien unter Berücksichtigung der schulischen Belange nach wirtschaftlichen Grundsätzen zu planen, zu bauen, zu unterhalten und zu bewirtschaften und die ca. 350 Schulen an die Behörde für Schule und Berufsbildung zu vermieten. GMH betreut für die Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg diverse Schulen im Süden Hamburgs, Hochschulen und kommunale Immobilien an unterschiedlichsten Standorten im Bundesland Hamburg.. Zudem wurde bei GMH die fachliche Kompetenz für den Bau und die Bewirtschaftung von Sportimmobilien gebündelt und damit für die Behörde für Inneres und Sport sowie die Hamburger Bezirksämter die Entwicklung unterschiedlichster Sportinfrastruktur-Projekte übernommen. SBH und GMH agieren sowohl als Realisierungsträger unmittelbar für die FHH als auch im Rahmen der beauftragten Projektsteuerung im Namen und auf Rechnung Anderer der FHH (z.B. BWFG). Die Bewirtschaftung der Liegenschaften umfasst auch bauliche Maßnahmen wie Instandsetzung, Neu- und Umbau. title: Germany – Internet service providers ISP – (TNW) Markt Bad Steben - Gigabit-RL 2.0 (2025) - Auswahlverfahren einer Dienstleistungskonzession im Wirtschaftlichkeitslückenmodell für die Planung, Errichtung und den Betrieb eines Gigabit-Netzes
description: Verhandlungsverfahren mit Teilnahmewettbewerb entsprechend § 12 KonzVgV i.V.m. § 14 Abs. 2, Abs. 3 Nr. 2, Nr. 3 VgV, § 119 Abs. 5 GWB (zweistufiges Verhandlungsverfahren) zur Be- stimmung eines Netzbetreibers für die Planung, die Errichtung und den Betrieb eines Gigabit- Netzes im Wirtschaftlichkeitslückenmodell in den ausgeschriebenen Ausbaugebieten nach Maßgabe der Richtlinie "Förderung zur Unterstützung des Gigabitausbau der Telekommunikati- onsnetze in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland" vom 31.03.2023 in der Fassung der 2. Änderung vom 13.01.2025 (nachfolgend "Gigabit-RL 2.0"). Aufgrund gegebener Grenznähe nimmt der Konzessionsgeber Binnenmarktrelevanz an und führt das Auswahlverfahren europaweit durch, obwohl der Schwellenwert nach § 106 GWB nicht er- reicht oder überschritten wird. Wesentliche Grundlage des Verfahrens sind die "Rahmenregelung der Bundesrepublik Deutsch- land zur Unterstützung des flächendeckenden Aufbaus von Gigabitnetzen" vom 01.08.2024 (nachfolgend "Gigabit-RR 2.0"), die Richtlinie "Förderung zur Unterstützung des Gigabitausbaus der Telekommunikationsnetze in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland" vom 31.03.2023 in der Fas- sung der 2. Änderung vom 13.01.2025 (nachfolgend Gigabit-RL 2.0) sowie die Mitteilung der Eu- ropäischen Union "Leitlinien für staatliche Beihilfen zur Förderung von Breitbandnetzen" vom 31.01.2023 (2023/C 36/01). Die ausgeschriebenen Adressen des Erschließungsgebietes sind nach Ergebnis der Markterkun- dung förderfähige unterversorgte Adressen im Sinne der Gigabit-RL 2.0. Aus diesem Grund soll dort auf Basis dieses Auswahlverfahrens ein Gigabit-Netz als technologieneutrale Netzbezeich- nung (Netz mit einer Breitbandversorgung von mindestens 1 Gbit/s symmetrisch zu Spitzenlast- zeitbedingungen für alle Endnutzer der ausgeschriebenen Adressen) in den unterversorgten Gebieten errichtet werden, wobei sich die Up- und Downloadraten mindestens verdoppeln müs- sen. Auf die Vorgaben der "B-Leistungsbeschreibung" inkl. deren Anlagen wird ergänzend ver- wiesen. Der Konzessionsgeber ordnet den ausgeschriebenen "Vertrag über die Weiterleitung von Zuwen- dungen im Rahmen des Gigabitausbaus in der Marktgemeinde Bad Steben zum Zwecke der Pla- nung, der Errichtung und des Betriebs eines gigabitfähigen Breitbandnetzes im Wirtschaftlichkeitslückenmodell nach der Richtlinie "Förderung zur Unterstützung des Gi- gabitausbaus der Telekommunikationsnetze in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland - Gigabit-Richt- linie des Bundes 2.0 (Gigabit-RL 2.0)" als eine Dienstleistungskonzession i.S.d. § 105 Abs. 1 Nr. 2 GWB ein. Der Konzessionsgeber überträgt damit die ihm als Aufgabe der Daseinsvorsorge oblie- gende Realisierung der Versorgung der Bevölkerung mit Gigabitanschlüssen auf den Konzessi- onsnehmer, welcher das Nutzungsrecht am Gigabit-Netz erhält und die Vergütung für seine Tätigkeit in erster Linie durch die Entgelte der Endkunden erhält, während der Konzessionsgeber lediglich einen Zuschuss zur Deckung der gegebenenfalls ausgewiesenen Wirtschaftlichkeitslü- cke leistet, welcher nach § 105 Abs. 1 Nr. 2 GWB einer Dienstleistungskonzession nicht entge- gensteht. Der Schwerpunkt der Tätigkeit des Konzessionsnehmers liegt auf der Dienstleistung des Betreibens des Breitbandnetzes über den Zeitraum von mindestens sieben Jahren. Der Konzessionsgeber ordnet weiter das zu planende, zu bauende und zu betreibende Gigabit- Netz auch als ein "öffentliches Kommunikationsnetz" i.S.d. Bereichsausnahme gemäß § 149 Nr. 8 GWB ein, so dass der 4. Teil des GWB nicht zur Anwendung kommt. Soweit in den Unterla- gen des Auswahlverfahrens auf Normen des 4. Teils des GWB verwiesen wird, begründet dies keinen Anspruch auf deren Anwendbarkeit.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Stadtwerke Frankenthal GmbH: Vergabe von Leistungen der Fachplanung für Technische Ausrüstung für die Errichtung eines Wärmenetzes in Frankenthal (Los 2)
description: Die Stadtwerke Frankenthal GmbH ist ein kommunales Energieversorgungsunternehmen mit Sitz in Frankenthal (Pfalz). Sie versorgt die Stadt Frankenthal sowie angrenzende Gemeinden im Rhein-Pfalz-Kreis. Der derzeitige Versorgungsschwerpunkt liegt auf der Gasversorgung. Im Zuge der Energiewende soll diese schrittweise durch ein modernes Fernwärmenetz ersetzt werden. Im Rahmen der Bundesförderung für effiziente Wärmenetze, Modul 1, wurde hierfür eine Machbarkeitsstudie erstellt. Auf Grundlage dieser Studie wurde das östliche Stadtgebiet als erstes Ausbaugebiet von insgesamt zwei Ausbaugebieten zum Wärmenetzausbau festgelegt. Das erste Ausbaugebiet umschließt den Wärmenetzausbau bis 2032 und das zweite Ausbaugebiet umschließt den Wärmenetzausbau bis 2045. Das zweite Ausbaugebiet dient ausschließlich als langfristiger Ziel- und Betrachtungsraum für den Netzausbau bis 2045. Die konkrete Umsetzung ist nicht Gegenstand der ausgeschriebenen Planungsleistungen und kann auf Grundlage der Planungsergebnisse in mehrere Teilgebiete und Ausbaustufen untergliedert werden. Das vorliegende Vergabeverfahren bezieht sich auf den flächendeckenden Ausbau des Wärmenetzes für das erste Ausbaugebiet. Im ersten Ausbaugebiet soll ein Wärmenetz errichtet werden, das seine Wärme aus einer vorgelagerten Wärmeerzeugung bezieht. Der Übergabepunkt zum Vorlieferanten soll hydraulisch entkoppelt und ausschließlich über einen Wärmetauscher thermisch mit der Transportleitung des Wärmevorlieferanten gekoppelt werden. Es handelt sich insgesamt um zwei Übergabepunkte bzw. -stationen die sich einmal nord- und südöstlich außerhalb der Stadtgrenzen befinden. Für das Wärmenetz ist vorgesehen, dass es im Endausbau im Zieljahr 2045 einen jährlichen Wärmeabsatz von etwa 100 GWh erreicht. Die ausgeschriebene Planungsleistung umfasst zunächst den flächendeckenden Wärmenetzausbau im östlichen Stadtgebiet bis zum Jahr 2032 (erstes Ausbaugebiet). Der angestrebte Wärmeabsatz im Endausbau soll anschließend über das zweite Ausbaugebiet bis zum Jahr 2045 erreicht werden. Die Stadtwerke Frankenthal GmbH beabsichtigen, Planungsleistungen für die Errichtung des Wärmenetzes zu vergeben. Für die zu vergebenden Planungsleistungen bis einschließlich Leistungsphase 4 HOAI wurde ein BEW-Modul 1-Förderantrag gestellt. Für die darauf aufbauenden Planungsleistungen wird voraussichtlich ein BEW-Modul 2-Förderantrag gestellt werden.

title: Germany – Paving and asphalting works – Neubau u. Sanierung Grund- u. Mittelschule Laufen - Pausenhof mit Leitungsbau
description: Baumaßnahme: Neubau und Sanierung Grund- und Mittelschule Laufen, Umbau Pausenhof mit Leitungsbau Bauort: Kohlhaasstraße 4, 83410 Laufen Geplanter Ausführungszeitraum: 12.03.2027 bis 14.05.2027 Im Zuge der o.a. Baumaßnahme ist vor dem Abbruch des bestehenden Turnhallengebäudes der zentrale Pausenhofbereich der Grundschule herzustellen. Der Leistungsumfang umfasst zunächst den Rückbau der vorhandenen Asphalt- und Betonsteinpflasterflächen einschließlich Einfassungen sowie des gebäudeseitigen Traufstreifens mit Kiesbettung. Das bestehende Gelände mit einem Höhenunterschied von ca. 1,50 m ist entsprechend der geplanten Höhenentwicklung durch Erdarbeiten und Geländemodellierung neu zu profilieren. Hierzu gehören Bodenabtrag, Abtransport und fachgerechte Entsorgung überschüssigen Bodenmaterials sowie die Herstellung der erforderlichen Frostschutz- und Tragschichten. Weiterhin umfasst die Maßnahme die Herstellung eines neuen Regenwasser- und Schmutzwasserkanals einschließlich der erforderlichen Anschlussleitungen sowie die Verlegung von Leerrohren für die unterirdische Elektroversorgung. Parallel zum Grundschulgebäude wird eine neue Feuerwehrzufahrt in Betonsteinpflasterbauweise einschließlich Einfassung mit Betonkantensteinen errichtet. Im zentralen Pausenhofbereich wird eine Spiel- und Bewegungsfläche mit unterschiedlichen Oberflächenbefestigungen hergestellt. Der westliche Teil erhält einen Belag aus großformatigem Betonsteinpflaster. Der östliche Teil wird als Spiel- und Bewegungsfläche mit EPDM-Kunststoffbelag hergestellt. Die Kunststoffbelagsflächen werden durch Betonsteinpflasterstreifen gegliedert und mit Betonkantensteinen eingefasst. Innerhalb der EPDM-Flächen ist ein neues Spielgerät einzubauen. Am südlichen Rand des Maßnahmenbereichs werden Natursteinblöcke zur Geländeabfangung eingebaut. Sämtliche Arbeiten sind unter Berücksichtigung des laufenden Schulbetriebs und der damit verbundenen Anforderungen an die Baustellenorganisation, Baustellensicherung und Verkehrssicherheit auszuführen. Die Fertigstellung der beschriebenen Leistungen ist bis spätestens 14.05.2027 vorgesehen.

Ziel der Maßnahme ist die planerische Vorbereitung und Umsetzung der Infrastrukturerschließung zur Erweiterung der technischen Perimetersicherung entlang der äußeren Flughafenumzäunung. Hierzu sind die baulichen und technischen Voraussetzungen für die Anbindung und Versorgung sicherheitstechnischer Einrichtungen zu schaffen. Die Leistungen umfassen die Generalplanung auf Grundlage der HOAI für: - Objektplanung Ingenieurbauwerke gemäß §§ 41 ff. HOAI, - Tragwerksplanung gemäß §§ 49 ff. HOAI, - Fachplanung Technische Ausrüstung gemäß §§ 53 ff. HOAI. Der Planungsumfang beinhaltet insbesondere Kabeltiefbau, Kabeltrassen, Kabelschutzrohranlagen, Kabelzugschächte, Querungen, Bestandseinbindungen, Energieversorgungs- und Dateninfrastruktur, Masten einschließlich Fundamente sowie die Einbindung der technischen Anlagen in die bestehende Infrastruktur des Flughafens. Die Beauftragung erfolgt stufenweise. Vorgesehen sind Leistungen der Objektplanung Ingenieurbauwerke und Technischen Ausrüstung in den Leistungsphasen 1 bis 8 sowie der Tragwerksplanung in den Leistungsphasen 1 bis 6.

title: Germany – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Beschaffung eines Netzleitsystems für die Stadtwerke Ratingen GmbH und die Stadtwerke Velbert GmbH
description: Die Stadtwerke Ratingen GmbH (nachfolgend: "Auftraggeberin" oder auch: "SWR") und die Stadtwerke Velbert GmbH (nachfolgend: "SWV") betreiben jeweils eigenständige Netzleitstellen für ihre Sparten Strom, Gas und Wasser. Um Synergien in Betrieb, Bereitschaftsdienst und Netzsteuerung zu realisieren, wird derzeit eine gemeinsame Gesellschaft, die Rheinisch-Bergische Verbundleitstelle GmbH (nachfolgend: "RBV"), gegründet, die künftig für beide Stadtwerke die operative Netzbetriebsführung für die Bestandssparten Strom, Gas, Wasser sowie ergänzend Wärme, übernehmen soll. Im Zuge dessen ist geplant, die bislang jeweils bestehenden Netzleitsysteme durch ein gemeinsames System zu ersetzen und perspektivisch der RBV zur Nutzung zu überlassen. Ziel ist es dabei, eine zukunftssichere, hochverfügbare und standardisierte Leitstellentechnologie als Basis der späteren Zusammenarbeit zu erhalten, die eine gemeinsame standortunabhängige Netzführung zwischen den Verbundleitstellen an den Standorten Velbert und Ratingen ermöglicht. Das zu beschaffende Netzleitsystem ist so auszulegen, dass es neben den aktuellen betrieblichen Anforderungen auch zukünftige Anforderungen aus der fortschreitenden Digitalisierung der Energienetze sowie der Energiewende nachhaltig erfüllen kann. Hierzu zählen insbesondere steigende Komplexität in der Netzführung, zunehmende Automatisierungs- und Analysebedarfe sowie die langfristige Erweiterbarkeit des Systems. Vor diesem Hintergrund beabsichtigt die Auftraggeberin, einen neuen Vertrag mit einem Dienstleister (nachfolgend: "Auftragnehmer") auf Basis der EVB-IT in eigener Sache sowie im Namen der SWV abzuschließen. Leistungsgegenstand sind neben der Bereitstellung der erforderlichen Software- und Hardwarelösungen insbesondere projektbezogene Leistungen wie die Implementierung, Migration, Schulung sowie verschiedenen Wartungs- und Serviceleistungen für beide Netzleitstellen. Einzelheiten zum Projekt lassen sich den Auftragsunterlagen entnehmen.

title: Germany – Social work services – KiTa-Belegplätze für Bonner Beschäftigte
description: Durch die Möglichkeit, einen Teil der Arbeitszeit im Home Office zu erbringen, rücken dezentrale Angebote der Kinderbetreuung zunehmend in den Fokus. Die Bafin beabsichtigt daher, KiTa-Belegplätze im U3- und Ü3-Bereich für ihre am Dienstsitz Bonn Beschäftigten in Bonn, im Rhein-Sieg-Kreis und im (südlichen) Köln zu beschaffen. Damit soll ein Unterstützungsangebot für Familien zur besseren Vereinbarkeit von Familie und Beruf geschaffen werden. Einzelheiten sind den Vergabeunterlagen zu entnehmen. Die Bafin legt großen Wert darauf, dass die Belegplätze möglichst in Wohnortnähe ihrer Beschäftigten zur Verfügung stehen, wobei sie sich bewusst ist, dass ein flächendeckendes Angebot an Belegplätzen am Markt derzeit nicht zur Verfügung steht. Daher müssen die im Rahmen dieses Verhandlungsverfahrens angesprochenen Unternehmen über mindestens vier Kindertageseinrichtungen je Losgebiet verfügen, bei denen ab 01.08.2028 prinzipiell Belegplätze durch die Auftraggeberin in Anspruch genommen werden können.

title: Belgium – Fire engines – Aankoop 2 Bosbrandwagens Type CCF
description: Hulpverleningszone Noord-Limburg beschikt over grote oppervlakten natuurgebieden (o.a. Nationaalpark Bosland) die elk jaar getroffen worden door natuurbranden (bos, heide,…). Deze ruwe terreinen vereisen gespecialiseerde voertuigen alle terrein om de manschappen, benodigde materiaal en vereiste bluswater ter plaatse te krijgen. Hulpverleningszone Noord-Limburg beschikt reeds over bosbrandvoertuigen type CCF en wil haar vloot uitbreiden met 2 bijkomende bosbrandvoertuigen type CCF 4x4 4.000 l, één voor de nieuwe brandweerpost Peer en één voor brandweerpost Lommel. Beide voertuigen zijn identiek. Het voertuig van brandweerpost Peer dient echter bijkomend uitgerust te worden met een sproeibalk en een systeem voor de dosering van zeep/detergent zodat dit voertuig buiten de winterperiode eveneens gebruikt kan worden voor kleine opdrachten “reinigen wegdek”. In het dossier zal eveneens een bepakkingslijst toegevoegd worden. De aanbieder dient hiervoor de eenheidsprijzen op te geven zodat i.f.v. het resterende budget het voertuig bijkomend uitgerust kan worden met brandbestrijdingsmaterialen. Overige materialen zullen door de Hulpverleningszone Noord-Limburg aangeleverd worden zodat de nodige ruimte voorzien kan worden tijdens de opbouw. De uniformiteit van inrichting van deze nieuwe voertuigen t.o.v. de reeds in gebruik zijnde CCF’s dient behouden te blijven (in samenspraak met de Hulpverleningszone tijdens de opbouw/inrichting). Al het voorgestelde materieel dient nieuw te zijn en elk element dient te voldoen aan de bijzondere interventievoorwaarden. De leverancier dient hiermee rekening te houden bij het voorstellen van het materieel. Het voertuig betreft een bosbrandwagen type CCF voor 4 personen. Het voertuig dient voorzien te zijn van een autoprotectiesysteem met een gereserveerde hoeveelheid water om in geval van nood de bemanning te kunnen beschermen. Het chassis moet van een goedgekeurd en gehomologeerd type zijn, aangepast aan het voertuigontwerp. Deze aanpassing wordt onderbouwd door een gewichtsberekening van het volledige concept, die bij de offerte wordt gevoegd. Bij levering zal het voertuig worden nagewogen. Indien het voertuig niet voldoet aan het vooropgestelde gewicht, kan dit aanleiding geven tot weigering van het product. Het aangeboden voertuig moet van het meest recente commerciële type zijn en geschikt zijn voor rijden en inzet op ruw terrein (oneffenheden in terrein, bospaden, losse zand, heuvels,…). Het voertuig moet op het moment van indiening van de offerte én bij levering volledig voldoen aan de geldende Europese en Belgische regelgeving.

title: Denmark – Office and computing machinery, equipment and supplies except furniture and software packages – Aftale om indkøb af hardware til mobilt setup og tilknyttede serviceydelser
description: Udbuddet vedrører anskaffelse af en mobil serverløsning til Hæren med tilhørende service og support. Løsningen skal anvendes til drift af Hærens eksisterende softwareprogrammer til træning af soldater i simulerede miljøer, herunder VBS og JCATS, og skal således understøtte gennemførelsen af simulationsbaserede træningsaktiviteter. Den samlede hardwareleverance omfatter: 1x Storage/Fog-server, 2x JCATS-servere, 2x NAS (Network Attached Storage), 2x UPS, 2x Routere 2x Switches. Serverne skal kunne anvendes til Hærens eksisterende softwareløsninger, og der skal kunne installeres tredjepartssoftware på serverne. Ud over hardwareleverancen omfatter anskaffelsen en standard Drifts- og Vedligeholdelsesaftale for Storage/Fog-serveren og JCATS-serverne. Aftalen skal sikre løbende drift og vedligeholdelse samt service og support af serverne i en periode på fem år fra kontraktens indgåelse. Drifts- og vedligeholdelsesaftalen skal bl.a. omfatte teknisk support fra kvalificeret supportpersonale, fjernfejlsøgning samt reparation eller udskiftning af defekte hardwarekomponenter, herunder nødvendige reservedele og arbejdsløn. Aftalen skal desuden omfatte adgang til producentens relevante firmware- og driveropdateringer samt sikkerhedsrettelser til serverne. Leverandøren skal registrere og følge op på supportsager og koordinere nødvendig hardwareafhjælpning frem til sagernes afslutning. Service- og supportydelserne skal kunne leveres i hele EU og skal omfatte både fjernsupport og nødvendig service på servernes placering, når fejl ikke kan afhjælpes ved fjernsupport. Service og support skal igangsættes senest 48 løbende timer efter modtagelse af ordregivers skriftlige anmodning, herunder i weekender og på helligdage. Igangsættelse kan ske ved fjernfejlsøgning. Hvis fjernfejlsøgningen viser behov for service på stedet, skal leverandøren uden unødigt ophold iværksætte denne og oplyse ordregiver om det forventede tidspunkt for service, support og afhjælpning. Alle ydelser og omkostninger, der er nødvendige for at opfylde kravene til Drifts- og Vedligeholdelsesaftalen, herunder reservedele, arbejdsløn, transport samt rejse- og opholdsudgifter ved service i EU, skal være omfattet af den tilbudte pris. De nærmere tekniske og funktionelle krav til hardwareleverancen samt kravene til drift, vedligeholdelse, service og support fremgår af udbudsmaterialet, herunder kravspecifikationen.

title: Mill Creek Section 205 Flood Risk Management Improvements
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Walla Walla District, is seeking information from interested business concerns capable of performing a construction project entitled Mill Creek Section 205 Flood Risk Management Improvements. The work is located in and near the Cities of Walla Walla and College Place, Walla Walla County, Washington. The Mill Creek Flood Control Project begins approximately two miles east of downtown Walla Walla and extends approximately seven miles downstream near College Place at the Gose Street Bridge. One hundred percent performance and payment bonds will be required. In accordance with RFO FAR Clause 52.228-1, a bid guarantee will also be required. The estimated magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. The anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction, with a corresponding small-business size standard of $45,000,000 in average annual receipts. This sources-sought notice is issued for market-research purposes only to identify business concerns with the capability to perform work of this nature, magnitude, and complexity.
