Identify special qualifications, certifications, key personnel, self-performance capabilities, equipment, and any proposed teaming arrangements relevant to the summary scope of work. 2. Relevant Experience. Provide at least three projects completed within the past seven years that are similar in scope, complexity, and magnitude. For each project, provide: -- Project title and location; -- Customer/owner; -- Contract value; -- Period of performance; -- Brief description of the work performed; -- The firm's role, including prime contractor, joint-venture member, or subcontractor; -- Major work self-performed by the firm; and -- Point of contact, including name, title, telephone number, and email address. 3. Bonding Capacity. Provide the firm's single-project bonding capacity and aggregate bonding capacity. 4. Business Size and Socioeconomic Status. Identify the firm's business size under NAICS 237990 and any applicable socioeconomic designations, including small business, Small Disadvantaged Business, 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) small business, Woman-Owned Small Business, Veteran-Owned Small Business, and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business. 5. SAM Registration. Provide the firm's Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and confirm whether its System for Award Management registration is active. Submit responses by email to: Chandra Crow, Contract Specialist U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Walla Walla District Email: Chandra.D.Crow@usace.army.mil Responses are due no later than 3:00 p.m. Pacific Time, December 4, 2026. Summary of Scope of Work: The Mill Creek Flood Control Project provides flood-risk management for the City of Walla Walla and adjacent areas in Walla Walla County, Washington. The project includes upstream channel, concrete channel, and downstream channel sections. The anticipated construction work includes flood-risk-management improvements and repairs at multiple locations along and within the upstream and downstream Mill Creek channel sections. Work may include: -- Raising existing levees by up to approximately three feet at five locations; -- Landward enlargement of levees while maintaining 2H:1V side slopes; -- Placement of additional gabion revetment at one location; -- Placement of additional riprap at transition areas, including ramp-to-levee and levee-to-bridge-abutment transitions; -- Construction of new concrete walls and/or raising of existing concrete walls at levee and bridge-transition locations; -- Construction of a concrete access ramp; -- Removal of trees and vegetation along the landside levee toe; -- Removal and in-kind replacement of existing fencing, as necessary to perform the work; -- Removal of a ceiling section in a covered portion of the existing concrete channel; -- Reinforcement of an existing timber-plank-covered support wall within the channel below an existing building; and -- Stabilization of two existing concrete-channel-wall sections using soil anchors and shotcrete facing. Work will occur on Federal and non-Federal/private property. The anticipated project may require work-site access planning, coordination with affected property owners and utilities, traffic control, in-kind replacement of fencing and utilities as required, and work within or adjacent to the active channel. The project is intended to improve Mill Creek system capacity by raising levees in low-assurance areas and to improve system reliability by repairing and reinforcing the concrete channel through downtown Walla Walla. title: Operations, Research, and Broad Innovative Technology Services (ORBIT) Request for Information (RFI) and Sources Sought Notice (SSN)
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. NO PROPOSALS ARE TO BE SUBMITTED IN RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE. The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center (JSC) Flight Operations Directorate (FOD) is hereby solicitating information from potential sources for the Operations, Research, and Broad Innovative Technology Services (ORBIT) solicitation. NASA JSC is issuing this RFI/SSN as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in, and the resources to support this requirement. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the type and method of procurement. A draft Statement of Work (dSOW) is in the attachment section for information and planning purposes and to allow industry the opportunity to verify reasonableness and feasibility of the requirement, as well as promote competition. NASA JSC is seeking capability statements from all interested parties, including all socioeconomic categories of Small Businesses (SB) and Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU)/Minority Institutions (MI) for the purposes of determining the appropriate level of competition and/or small business subcontracting goals for ORBIT. Vendors are encouraged to demonstrate capabilities as a prime, subcontractor and/or teaming partner. The Government reserves the right to consider a Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), HUBZone, Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, and Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) business set-aside based on responses received. Respondents are requested to provide informed input on realistic and appropriate SB subcontracting and/or participation goals for the specific requirement. This type of feedback supports NASA�s market research and helps ensure the acquisition strategy is aligned with actual industry capability. Industry feedback is requested for: 1. SB Subcontracting goals; 2. Barriers that may limit SB participation, such as certifications, unique technical requirements, security needs, specialized tools, or high-risk performance areas and/or 3. Strategies to increase SB participation, including: � Breaking requirements into smaller components � Identifying areas appropriate for subcontracting � Considering teaming or mentor prot�g� approaches The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541512, Computer Systems Design Services, and the corresponding small business size standard is $34 million, calculated in accordance with 13 CFR 121.104. ORBIT Description: The proposed ORBIT contract will provide mission engineering, spaceflight-enabling, mission support, and advanced technology services to NASA's Flight Operations Directorate (FOD) at Johnson Space Center (JSC) and its mission partners. It is anticipated that the ORBIT will be a multiple-award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract vehicle with Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) task orders. This acquisition will establish a follow-on contract vehicle to succeed the Mission Enabling Support Contract MESC-IDIQ contracts, encompassing the legacy and a subset of those requirements including partial scope of MESC-B, which are scheduled to expire on September 30, 2027. The follow- on contract restructures the acquisition strategy to better align functionally related capability areas as part of a single procurement , reduces the contract administration burden on the Government, improves small business participation and competition at the task order level, and provides a more efficient and flexible contracting mechanism for the delivery of the following Functional Area Requirements identified in the dSOW: � Functional Area 1 - Mission and Systems Engineering Support � Functional Area 2 - Technical Evaluation, Analysis, and Independent Assessment � Functional Area 3 Specialized IT and Operations � Functional Area 4 - Advanced Mission R&D No solicitation exists; therefore, do not request a copy of the solicitation. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on SAM.gov. Interested firms are responsible for monitoring this website for the release of any solicitation or synopsis. Interested firms having the required capabilities necessary to meet the above requirement described herein should submit a capability statement of no more than 10 pages indicating the ability to perform all aspects of the effort. Capability Statement: Interested firms having the required capabilities necessary to meet the above requirement should indicate the ability to perform all aspects of the effort, and include the following information: 1. Technical - Describe your company's overall skills, experience, and capabilities to perform the work of the ORBIT dSOW. Please identify specific dSOW sections where your company could provide the stated capability by way of Attachment 1 - Vendor Capability Matrix at the end of this announcement. If subcontracting or if a joint venture is anticipated, organizations should address the anticipated administrative and management structure of such arrangements (if this information is known at this time). Also address what elements of work would be performed by the prime or joint venture partners and which elements would be performed by subcontractors. 2. General � a. What additional documents would you like to see on the ORBIT contract website or included in the Technical Library? b. What barriers or obstacles do you foresee to potentially bidding on this contract? Can you identify any Government acquisition approaches that would increase the competitiveness of this procurement? What innovations might you propose in the performance of this contract or contract structure? c. What innovations might you propose in the performance of this contract or contract structure? 3. Company-Specific Information - Responses must include the following: a. Company�s name, address, and a point of contact (name, e-mail address, and address) b. Unique Entity Identifier number and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code c. Number of years in business d. Size of business i. Average annual revenue for past three years ii. Number of employees iii. Whether the firm is a Large, SB, Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), HUBZone, WOSB, Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB), SDVOSB, HBCU/MI, and/or 8a e. Ownership, affiliate information (as applicable) including parent company and joint venture partners f. If you plan to propose as a prime or as a subcontractor; g. A list of contracts covering the past three years with emphasis on work performed for the United States Federal Government. Please provide contract numbers, if your firm was a prime or subcontractor, contract type, dollar value of each procurement, and customer point of contact (address, phone, and email). If work was performed as a subcontractor, please indicate percentage of work/subcontract dollar value. If the contract(s) were IDIQ, please indicate the number of task orders awarded and the total dollar value of those task orders. h. Company�s specific capabilities that are relevant to the requirements contemplated above. It is not sufficient to provide general brochures or generic information. This RFI/SSN is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. Respondents deemed fully qualified will be considered in any resultant solicitation for the requirement. All responses must be submitted electronically via email to the Contracting Officer at jsc-orbit-procurement@mail.nasa.gov no later than 5:00 PM CENTRAL DAYLIGHT TIME on October 05, 2026. Please reference �ORBIT Sources Sought� in the subject line of any response. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at : https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurem

Please refer to Table 1 for disposal site, dredge windows, and other project related information. Upland disposal placement for San Joaquin River and Sacramento River Deep Water Ship Channels (DWSC) are at contractor furnished upland beneficial reuseuse sites or at the various Government-furnished sites located along the channels. If a Government-furnished site is chosen, the and the material shall be pumped to the sites based on various pumping distances and depth of material. Surveys shall also be conducted prior to and following completion of dredging per SPN�s Light Monitoring Protocol. For Oakland Harbor, in addition to the standard alternative of ocean disposal at SF-DODS or placement at a beneficial use site, approximately 250,000 cubic yards of dredged material may be placed at a nearshore placement site shallow depths (-5 to +5 ft MLLW) near Emeryville Crescent State Marine Reserve in shallow water depths ranging from -5 to +5 ft MLLW. title: Ireland – Development of residential real estate – Cork City Council Housing Programme 2026-28
description: The Cork City Council Housing Programme 2026-2028 will form part of the City Council’s housing delivery action plan under the Government’s Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030 (DHBC)1, although this procurement process may include schemes that will be delivered beyond the lifetime of the DHBC. The Government’s DHBC sets out an overall ambition to activate the supply of 300,000 homes over the lifetime of the plan, including an annual average delivery of 12,000 new social homes and 15,000 starter home supports. There are significant targets to be delivered in Cork City and in this regard the Cork City Council Housing Programme 2026-2028 is a major part of the Council’s delivery plan under the DHBC and any subsequent national housing delivery programme. Cork City Council proposes to deliver and facilitate the delivery of social, starter homes and mixed tenure schemes in delivery of its housing programme over the coming years and therefore invites proposals from Candidates which can deliver social, starter homes, or mixed tenure schemes, to include new build construction, conversion of existing residential or non- residential properties, or schemes which form part of a larger development. Starter homes or mixed tenure schemes may include provision for cost-rental delivery in partnership with an Approved Housing Body (AHB).

description: The objective of this Procurement Procedure is for Radboud University Medical Center (Radboudumc) to select and contract a single Contractor for the supply, installation, commissioning, training, and maintenance of a Confocal Microscope System for use by RTC Light Microscopy. Through this procurement, Radboudumc intends to expand its existing microscopy infrastructure with a user-friendly and future-proof system capable of delivering rapid, high-resolution three-dimensional (3D) imaging. The intended system shall support the current and future research needs of Radboudumc and contribute to maintaining a state-of-the-art microscopy facility. The microscope system will be installed as a shared research facility within RTC Light Microscopy and will be centrally managed by the UMC. Following installation, commissioning, and the completion of the required user training, the system will be made available to authorised and qualified Radboudumc staff and researchers. The Contracting Authority seeks a reliable and sustainable solution that combines high imaging performance with ease of use, operational continuity, and long-term support throughout the lifecycle of the system.

title: Custodial Services at Altus AFB
description: POSTAWARD NOTICE Solicitation FA441926Q0002 was posted via SAM.gov on 2 July 2026. A total of twenty-four (24) quotes were received in response to FA441926Q0002. Below is the award information: a. Contractor: MAGADIA CONSULTING, INC. b. Award Date: 20 November 26 c. Contract Number: FA441926D0002 d. Total Evaluated Price: $ 4,475,979.42 e. Technical Rating: Acceptable f. Past Performance Confidence Rating: Recent � Very Relevant -Substantial Confidence g. Decision Summary: Pricing has been determined fair and reasonable. As a result, IDIQ Contract FA441927D0002 with a TEP of $4,475,979.42 and a contract ceiling of $9,000,000.00 will be awarded to Magadia Consulting, Inc. (CAGE: 59SC7 / UEI: PJDZNFZVJJ87). An initial Task Order will be issued concurrently with basic contract award to obligate the guaranteed minimum contract minimum of $60,000.00. 3. As stated in �Attachment 4 � Evaluation Factors� The evaluation will begin with a cursory review of all submissions for completeness. If an offeror fails to submit a complete submission, including a complete SF 1449, bid schedule, technical volume, and past performance records, the offeror will be rendered non-responsive, and no further evaluation will be conducted. The evaluation team will rank complete quotes by Total Evaluated Price (TEP) from lowest to highest (see below detailed explanation on the calculation of TEP). The evaluation will begin by evaluating the technical submissions of the three (3) lowest ranked quotes. If the technical submissions of the three (3) lowest ranked offers are acceptable, the evaluation process will proceed to the next step. If any of the three (3) lowest ranked offers results in an unacceptable rating, the evaluation team will evaluate the next lowest offeror, as initially ranked TEP, for technical acceptability. Evaluation at this step will continue until there are three (3) technically acceptable offerors. The three (3) lowest priced, technically acceptable, responsive offers will then be evaluated for past performance. If these offers do not yield at least two (2) offerors with an overall rating of Substantial or Satisfactory Confidence, the evaluation process will continue until a minimum of two (2) offerors with an overall rating of Substantial or Satisfactory Confidence are identified or all quotes are evaluated. The Source Selection Authority shall then make an integrated assessment to render the best value award decision. The Source Selection Authority may also make the determination that it is in the best interest of the Government to evaluate all offerors for technical acceptability and past performance prior to rendering the best value award decision. While the Government will strive for maximum objectivity, the acquisition process, by its nature, is subjective; and therefore, professional judgment is implicit throughout the entire process. Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to all required terms and conditions, includes all required representations and certifications, meets all requirements set forth in the solicitation and provides the best value to the Government. The submission ranked first (1st) based on Factor 1was found to be non-responsive and was removed from competition. The submissions ranked second (2nd), third (3rd) and fourth (4th) based on Factor 1: Price all received Technical Rating: Acceptable based on the criteria in Factor 2. All three were then evaluated for Past Performance using the criteria outlined in Factor 3. All three were found to be recent and relevant. The evaluation determined one (1) offer to be Satisfactory Confidence, one (1) offer to be Neutral Confidence and one (1) to be Substantial Confidence. Magadia Consulting Inc. was determined to be the responsible offeror whose quote represents the best value, defined as providing the greatest confidence that the vendor will satisfy the Government's requirements affordably.

title: 48--MANIFOLD ASSEMBLY P
TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: PBI High-Temperature Hollow Fiber Membranes
description: Polybenzimidazole (PBI) High-Temperature Hollow Fiber Membranes offer a practical way to improve separation efficiency in process environments where standard polymer membranes often lose performance or durability. The platform combines high-temperature operation, chemical resistance and compact hollow-fiber design in a membrane system that can help users recover hydrogen, separate carbon dioxide and process difficult liquid streams with lower energy demand and a smaller equipment footprint than many conventional approaches. Because the fibers are formed from a robust PBI material and engineered with an integrated thin selective layer, the technology is well suited for organizations seeking stronger performance in demanding energy, chemical and water treatment settings. How it Works The membrane works like a selective gate built into a very small hollow strand. A mixed gas or liquid flows across the fiber, and the thin outer layer allows some molecules to pass through more readily than others, while the porous support beneath it gives the fiber strength and a path for transport. The disclosed fabrication process forms that selective layer and support structure in one step, then can add heat treatment or a thin sealing layer to improve stability and sharpen separation performance. Technical Description The polybenzimidazole invention is centered on a method for making asymmetric hollow fiber membranes from polybenzimidazole, a polymer valued for strong thermal and chemical stability. A PBI dope solution and a bore fluid are extruded through a spinneret, then passed through an optional air gap and into a water coagulation bath, which forms a hollow fiber with an integrated selective layer and a porous support structure. The process can produce nearly defect-free selective layers, and the patent states that selective layer thickness can be controlled from about 0.1 to 5 �m, with examples demonstrating thicknesses down to about 160 nm and one example near 0.38 �m. A major technical advantage is control over membrane microstructure and durability. PBI High-Temperature Hollow Fiber Membranes emphasize macrovoid-free fibers, which are important because macrovoids create weak points that can fail under high temperature and pressure. The membranes can be thermally annealed or chemically crosslinked to improve solvent resistance and stability, and a defect-sealing layer can be added to improve selectivity without changing the core fiber architecture. In demonstrated gas-separation modules, the technology showed hydrogen permeance above 100 GPU, with one example reporting 242 GPU at 250 �C and hydrogen/carbon dioxide selectivity of 19.1, while long-term testing in wet syngas with 20 ppm H2S showed stable performance over 40 days. The patent also states that the membranes can operate up to about 400 �C and are suitable for gas, vapor and liquid separations including hydrogen purification, carbon capture, brine treatment and organic solvent separations. Advantages Operates at temperatures that are too demanding for many conventional polymer membranes Resists harsh chemical exposure including steam and sulfur-containing gases compact module design enables smaller equipment footprint easier scaling than ceramic membranes higher throughput without compromising permeability, selectivity or membrane area cost Combines selectivity and structural support in one integrated membrane architecture Supports both gas and liquid separation opportunities across multiple industries Reduces overall hydrogen purification costs Has already been tested in relevant operating environments rather than remaining only a laboratory concept Market Applications Energy and Power generation (hydrogen production, pre-combustion carbon capture, syngas cleanup) Oil and Gas (refining, natural gas processing, produced water treatment) Chemical and Petrochemical Processing (process gas separation, solvent dehydration, feedstream cleanup) Industrial Water and Wastewater (high-salinity brines, water purification, water and acid separation) Advanced Fuels (Fischer-Tropsch processing, fuel conversion, synthesis gas upgrading) Specialty Manufacturing (organic solvent recovery, pharmaceutical and fine chemical separations) Development Status: TRL 5 US Patent No. 10,071,345 LA-UR-26-24561 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. For specific discussions, please contact licensing@lanl.gov. description: VA AIR AMBULANCE BROKER WITH SUPPORTING GROUND TRANSPORTATION VIRTUAL INDUSTRY DAY NOTICE December 10-11, 2026 Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Veterans Transportation Program (VTP) Network Contracting Office (NCO) 20 1. Purpose The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Transportation Program (VTP), will host an Industry Day to engage with air and ground transportation brokers capable of providing Air Ambulance Broker with Supporting Ground Transportation Services nationwide. This Industry Day is not a request for proposal. It is a market research tool being used to determine potential firms capable of providing the services described herein prior to determining the method of acquisition. The purpose of this session is to: Provide industry with an overview of the upcoming Air Ambulance Broker Services requirement. Offer vendors an opportunity to ask questions and provide feedback prior to release of the solicitation. Support industry�s understanding of VTP�s operational needs, compliance requirements, and contracting expectations as defined within the Performance Work Statement (PWS). 2. Requirement Overview The upcoming procurement will establish multiple-award IDIQ contracts for nationwide fixed-wing and rotary-wing air ambulance broker services, supported by ancillary ground transportation services which refers to transportation services used to transport Veterans between airports, healthcare facilities, Veterans' residences, and other approved destinations. Ground transportation modes may include private vehicles, taxis, rideshare services, wheelchair-accessible vans and shuttles, ambulances, and other specialized transportation services necessary to meet a Veteran's mobility, accessibility, or medical transportation needs. Key highlights include: 24/7/365 availability including holidays Compliance with CAMTS/NAAMTA transport standards Real-time communication and documentation via VA Mandated Transportation Software Quality Control and subcontractor oversight requirements Support for advanced life support, life support, basic life support, critical care transport and stretcher transports 3.
